findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the source and meaning of the envelope's 'namespace version' identity component (e.g. the discovery contract/schema version) so an executor can compute it deterministically without a clarifying question.
evidence: 'identity covers material, code/ref, effective-policy snapshot, prompt and contract, model/mode, topology, input context, dependencies, and namespace version'
No section defines the source/provenance of 'namespace version' (E2 signals 1/2 — a referenced identity field with no stated source)
findings.finding: 'namespace version' is listed as a component of the envelope's digest-complete identity, but the plan never states where it comes from or what it represents, even though it is load-bearing for the 'legacy checkpoints are never read as new successes' guarantee (a bumped namespace version is the natural staleness discriminator).
scenarios: An executor implementing the envelope codec must invent what feeds 'namespace version' and how legacy/stale detection uses it, risking either always-miss or accidental collisions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the budget-shed loop re-evaluates projected spend against the cap AFTER cascading a shed unit's dependents into `skipped` (stop-when-fits), so the shed set is minimal and the (rank,id) determinism is unambiguous under cascades.
evidence: Plan: 'deterministic order: ascending dependency rank, then stable unit id ... shedding a unit also sheds its unmet dependents as skipped'
AC5 fixes order + identical-set + zero-rejected + omission-uncapped but is silent on whether the cap check re-runs after a cascade

Prior-art sizing.shed_to_budget uses a while-loop that re-projects sheddable spend after each pop (sizing.py:624), i.e. it re-evaluates fit; the kernel's cascade adds dependents the loop did not pop, so the analogous re-check semantics need stating
findings.finding: The interaction between positive-budget shedding and dependency cascades is under-specified: when shedding a unit cascades its unmet dependents into `skipped`, the plan does not state whether the shed loop then re-evaluates remaining projected spend against the cap (so it stops once the kept set fits) or whether the dependents' freed budget is reclaimed. AC5 asserts a deterministic, identical shed set but not the fit-recomputation semantics when a shed cascades.
findings.location: Approach ('explicit positive-budget shedding ... shedding a unit also sheds its unmet dependents as skipped'); AC5
scenarios: A low-rank unit with several dependents is shed to meet the cap; the cascade removes more projected spend than the single unit, so a later, otherwise-sheddable unit need not have been shed — but the plan does not say the loop stops early once the kept set fits.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the new discovery executor against workflow/executor.py (graphlib.static_order scheduling, succeeded|failed|skipped step outcomes, copy-on-write RunState, RunRecorder replay) and ADR 0065's Burr tripwire — state explicitly why a second dependency-aware scheduler is warranted rather than reusing/extending those primitives.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py:1-4 'runs a validated workflow's steps in graphlib.static_order (topological) order'
src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py:156 'status: str = "succeeded"  # succeeded | failed | skipped'
docs/adr/0065-burr-adoption-tripwire.md:14-23 tripwire fails if the executor 'imports asyncio / concurrent / threading ...' — forcing a deliberate decision rather than accreting a bespoke scheduler
The plan's 'Boundaries and Rationale' reconciles sizing/pass1/generation helpers in detail but is silent on the existing topological executor and the Burr tripwire ADR
findings.finding: The plan stands up a new hand-rolled dependency-aware execution kernel ('the executor owns dependency-aware scheduling ... ascending dependency rank ... shedding a unit also sheds its unmet dependents as skipped') without reconciling against the repo's existing DAG executor and its explicit anti-bespoke-scheduler ADR. src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py already schedules units in graphlib.static_order (topological), records per-step outcomes as 'succeeded | failed | skipped', models run state as immutable copy-on-write RunState, and persists through a RunRecorder seam with crash-recovery replay — the same scheduling/outcome/recorder primitives the discovery kernel reinvents. ADR 0065 (the Burr adoption tripwire) is the repo's test-enforced position that dependency-aware / parallel scheduling of independent units must stay graphlib-thin or adopt Burr, NOT grow a second hand-rolled scheduler. The plan never mentions graphlib, workflow/executor.py, or ADR 0065.
findings.location: Approach / Boundaries and Rationale — 'the executor owns dependency-aware scheduling ... deterministic order: ascending dependency rank'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer asks why review gets a second scheduler instead of reusing the graphlib executor's outcome/recorder/RunState primitives
The discovery executor later needs parallel scheduling (it already fans out concurrently in run_pass1 via a worker pool), tripping exactly the ADR 0065 trigger the plan never engaged
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prior-art paragraph in Boundaries and Rationale that names workflow/executor.py and ADR 0065, explains why the review discovery kernel cannot reuse the existing topological executor's scheduling/outcome/recorder primitives (e.g. review-specific typed outcomes and digest-complete envelope), and confirms the design stays within — or deliberately relaxes — the Burr tripwire's no-bespoke-scheduler constraint.

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the per-unit dependency graph / skip-on-missing-dependency / dependency-rank machinery against a CURRENT done-definition, or scope this story to the empty-graph independent-fan-out substrate and defer the dependency edge (and its AC5 digest coverage) to the migration story that first composes a dependent unit.
evidence: Plan: 'for both current gates the graph is EMPTY and scheduling is independent fan-out'
Plan: 'introduced as the shared-substrate contract, NOT because a current gate exhibits such an edge'
Plan: 'The typed edge exists so migration stories composing a unit that consumes another's result express a skip-on-missing dependency' (hypothetical future consumer)

Codebase: `plan_review/pass1.run_pass1` fans chunks/agent criteria out INDEPENDENTLY (a failed chunk only increments `chunk_errors`); `code_review/batch_runner.CodeReviewBatchRunner.run` runs 'EACH included criterion's own prompt ... aggregating their findings' — no cross-unit dependency exists in either live gate
Justification is self-referential: AC5's dependency-digest stability is only needed because the graph field exists
findings.finding: The per-unit dependency graph, dependency-rank ordering, `skipped`-with-dependency-reason outcome, and dependent-shedding are introduced with zero current call-sites: the plan states both current gates have an EMPTY graph and admits the edge is added 'NOT because a current gate exhibits such an edge,' justified only by hypothetical future migration units — a YAGNI / Rule-of-Three (premature-abstraction) concern.
findings.location: Approach + 'Boundaries and Rationale' (dependency-graph paragraph); AC3, AC5
scenarios: Both gates ship on this kernel while every unit graph is empty; the dependency machinery (rank ordering, skip-on-missing, dependent-shedding, digest coverage) is dead weight carried and tested against no real consumer until an unscheduled future migration

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the discovery-vs-decision kernel split and its import/export boundary in an ADR or design-doc update (or add a covering AC that requires it).
evidence: 'Add a narrow shared discovery kernel as a NEW `discovery` submodule under `rebar.llm.review_kernel`, independent of that package's four-pass DECISION kernel'
No Acceptance Criterion or body sentence commits to recording this decision in an ADR or design doc
findings.finding: The plan introduces a genuinely novel architectural pattern — a second, separate kernel family (`discovery`) living alongside the existing four-pass DECISION kernel under `rebar.llm.review_kernel` — but names no ADR, AGENTS.md, or design-doc update to capture why review_kernel now hosts two independent kernels and where the boundary lies.
scenarios: A future contributor sees two kernels under review_kernel and cannot tell from any doc why discovery is separate, whether it may depend on the decision kernel, or which future gate work belongs where.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC or Boundaries line: record the two-kernel architecture and the additive/no-cross-import invariant in an ADR (or a review_kernel design-doc/AGENTS.md note) so the boundary is documented, not just plan-scoped.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the discovery-kernel gate migration against ADR 0003 (workflow-as-gate) — state whether the discovery kernel runs inside, alongside, or instead of the workflow-engine gate migration, so the two do not converge on incompatible execution models.
evidence: docs/adr/0003-workflow-as-gate.md:4 'Epic Migrate the LLM gates onto the workflow engine'
docs/adr/0003-workflow-as-gate.md:27 'Express an LLM gate as an engine workflow ... the workflow-as-gate pattern'
The plan describes migrating gates onto the discovery kernel but never references ADR 0003 or the workflow engine as the gates' migration destination
findings.finding: The plan positions the discovery kernel as the migration target for the review gates ('RP-06's migration stories move the gates onto' it) but does not reconcile with ADR 0003 (workflow-as-gate), the standing epic that migrates the LLM review gates ONTO the workflow engine. Building an independent execution kernel for the same gates is potentially a divergent second migration path; the plan should state how the discovery kernel relates to (or supersedes / defers to) workflow-as-gate.
findings.location: Approach — 'a NEW discovery submodule' and Boundaries — 'RP-06's migration stories move the gates onto'
scenarios: The workflow-as-gate epic and the RP-06 discovery-kernel migration proceed in parallel and converge on incompatible execution models for the same two gates
